Supported findings:

- The run commit changes only `frontend/src/methodology.md`; Rust inputs, Dockerfiles, and workflows match the previous successful run. [Commit](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/commit/521c6daef251d71b96e33f3f0d880396eb94194b)
- Frontend changes trigger the entire release. The composite builds backend, frontend, migration, and CLI images sequentially. [Workflow](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/blob/521c6daef251d71b96e33f3f0d880396eb94194b/.github/workflows/release.yml), [composite action](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/blob/521c6daef251d71b96e33f3f0d880396eb94194b/.github/actions/build-images/action.yml)
- PR #98 explicitly states: “The existing workflow still builds all four images, including Rust, on frontend-only changes.” It only separated Dockerfiles. [PR #98](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/98)
- Previous run’s same composite took **4m34s** (10:52:34–10:57:08 UTC), with **5m46s** total workflow time. This run’s extended duration therefore has no corresponding build-configuration change. [Previous run](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/actions/runs/40310754096)
- This is native AMD64 only. Historical QEMU ARM slowness was addressed in #78 and automatic ARM builds removed in #80. #78 reported a **19m24s cold native backend build**, useful historical context but not a directly comparable benchmark. [PR #78](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/78), [PR #80](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/80)

Hypotheses requiring runtime logs:

- Cache restore/export delays or a cache miss could explain the difference. All four builds use the same architecture cache scope; this merits inspection, but source alone does not establish cache failure.
- A cold Rust build could take this long: the Dockerfile builds release dependencies and application with `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2`. However, frontend-only changes do not alter Rust `COPY` inputs, so recompilation is not demanded by this commit.
- Source control cannot distinguish compilation, registry operations, cache transfer, or a stalled action. No evidence supports blaming #98 for this particular regression.

The run appears delayed inside the image-build action, most likely during the later backend variants. The exact operation remains unconfirmed. [Current run](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/actions/runs/40312266098)

Observed evidence:

- The composite action started at **11:04:30 UTC** and remained active around **11:24**.
- New cache indexes appeared at **11:04:46** and **11:05:33**. Their sizes and ordering resemble the previous run’s backend and frontend exports.
- The latest recorded cache access was **11:05:34**. This establishes no subsequent recorded cache activity; it does **not** establish that compilation or other work stopped.
- The previous run completed the same action in **4m34s**. This commit changes only methodology text. [Previous run](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/actions/runs/40310754096), [commit](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/commit/521c6daef251d71b96e33f3f0d880396eb94194b)

The cache pattern suggests the frontend build reached its cache export around 11:05:33, placing the delay afterward—likely in the migration or CLI build, or associated cache/registry operations. The action runs backend → frontend → migration → CLI sequentially. This is an inference, not a confirmed substep diagnosis. [Build action](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/blob/521c6daef251d71b96e33f3f0d880396eb94194b/.github/actions/build-images/action.yml)

The broader inefficiency is confirmed: frontend-only changes still build all four images. PR #98 explicitly preserved that behavior. It explains why a documentation change enters these builds, but does not explain today’s unusual delay. [PR #98](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/98)

Live logs remain unavailable through the API (`BlobNotFound`), so there is currently insufficient evidence to distinguish a stalled build, cache transfer, or registry operation.
